newsitem.title: USA: Cabletron cites slow Europe sales for soft Q1.
newsitem.headline: Cabletron cites slow Europe sales for soft Q1.

text.p: Cabletron Systems Inc said Monday its first quarter results failed to meet expectations primarily because of very weak European sales and insufficient production of its new high-end switching products.
Earlier this month, Cabletron warned its earnings would fall well short of analysts' estimates, but offered only sketchy explanations about the reasons for the shortfall.

Cabletron today reported net income of $58.8 million or $0.38 per share, up slightly from $57.1 million or $0.37 a year ago. Prior to Cabletron's June 2 warning, analysts had expected the company to earn $0.50 per share in the quarter.
In a press release announcing the company's first quarter results, Cabletron said European sales were "substantially below target" for the quarter.
Cabletron said it had undertaken efforts to address performance issues in Europe but noted summer is a soft period in Europe "and immediate improvement is not anticipated."

The company also said that demand was strong for its high-end switching products, but it was unable to match production of its new SmartSwitch 6000 line with demand, resulting in lost sale opportunities.
Cabletron said it was working with suppliers to increase SmartSwitch production but said "product availability issues will continue through the second quarter."
Sales for mature product lines declined more than expected in the period, exacerbating the problem, it said.
